- When sentiment is high (≥0.6), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-term (10–20 day) trends; apply 1–2% downward correction for 10–20 day horizons.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to correct; add 2–3% downward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.5 for 2+ consecutive days.
- Model underestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment >0.5.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 75 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes or sentiment rebounds.
